metadata.case_name: LEUNG KWOK KEUNG, JOHNAKIN v. LEUNG IU WA

plaintiff.occupation_before: Service Manager (Hong Kong and China) (Service Manager of Medical Imaging Department of General Electric Co in Hong Kong)
plaintiff.occupation_after: Working in father's amusement game centre (quasi-managerial)
plaintiff.education_level: Diploma in radio and telecommunication technology; higher certificate in electronic engineering; commenced MBA (two years) but abandoned

injuries.description: fractures of skull, depressed over the calvarium but multiple at the base compounded into the nose causing cerebral spinal fluid rhinorrhoea and into the ears.
injuries.body_part: skull / anterior cranial fossa / paranasal sinuses
source: The Plaintiff's head injury was complicated by fractures of skull, depressed over the calvarium but multiple at the base compounded into the nose causing cerebral spinal fluid rhinorrhoea and into the ears.
injuries.icd_description: Multiple fractures involving skull or facial bones

injuries.description: severe right frontal lobe contusion of the brain leading to extensive oedema, subarachnoid haemorrhage and midline shift of the brain and damage to the hypothalamus resulting in diabetes insipidus.
source: The Plaintiff had severe right frontal lobe contusion of the brain leading to extensive oedema, subarachnoid haemorrhage and midline shift of the brain and damage to the hypothalamus resulting in diabetes insipidus.

injuries.description: severe loss of brain cells (encephalomalacia) at right frontal lobe
source: The Plaintiff has severe loss of brain cells (encephalomalacia) at right frontal lobe and mild hoarseness of voice.

injuries.description: frontal-basal damage to the olfactory nerves
source: As a result of frontal-basal damage to the olfactory nerves, the Plaintiff has bilateral loss of smell (anosmia) and has a persistent bizarre smell…which will be permanent.

injuries.description: intracranial haematoma (associated with skull fractures) treated with emergency decompressive craniectomy
source: A CT scan showed that he had fractures of skull with intracranial haematoma. He was then transferred to Prince of Wales Hospital. There, emergency decompressive craniectomy was performed by the neurosurgical team.
The Plaintiff has post-traumatic epileptic seizures, which may recur from time to time, so that he will have to take anticonvulsant for life.
injuries.icd_description: Epilepsy due to injuries to the head

injuries.description: two permanent surgical scars at the front of the head with visible bony defects under the skin
source: The Plaintiff has 2 permanent surgical scars at the front of the head with visible bony defects under the skin.
injuries.icd_description: Fracture of squama of frontal bone of skull

source: The Plaintiff subsequently developed diabetes insipidus.

manifestations.description: bilateral loss of smell (anosmia) and persistent bizarre smell (permanent)
post-traumatic epileptic seizures (requires lifelong anticonvulsant medication)
requires lifelong administration of anticonvulsants (approx. cost HK$1,000 per month in private sector)
2 permanent surgical scars at the front of the head with visible bony defects under the skin
urinary and faecal incontinence (noted as experienced post-injury)
mild impairment of intellectual and memory function

personality change: lack of foresight, impaired judgement, difficulty making appropriate decisions, impatience, impaired impulse control, short-temper, behaviour not appropriate to social convention, lack of care for external appearance, tired easily, lack of initiative and motivation, restricted emotional response, stubbornness, inability to manage finances
loss of taste (as consequence of loss of smell)

treatments_received: Admission and intubation at United Christian Hospital
CT scan showing skull fractures and intracranial haematoma
Transfer to Prince of Wales Hospital
Intracranial pressure monitoring catheter inserted and later removed
Repair of fracture base of skull (1 June 1999)
Repair of cerebral spinal fluid leakage (8 June 1999)
Intensive Care Unit care for 9 days
treatments_future: Psychiatric counselling (24 sessions recommended by Dr CHUNG)
Continuation of anticonvulsant medication lifelong (public sector supply with prescription charges)
Plastic surgery of bony defects discussed but not recommended (opinion of Dr YU/Dr CHUNG)

losses.description: Bilateral loss of smell (anosmia) with persistent bizarre smell, permanent.
Two permanent surgical scars at the front of the head with visible bony defects under the skin.
Mild impairment of intellectual and memory function.
Persistent personality disturbance (impulsivity, impaired judgement, poor impulse control, impatience, lack of initiative, restricted emotional response) due to head trauma.
Severe loss of brain cells (encephalomalacia) at right frontal lobe.
Needed daily, ongoing care of his wife in the period after the accident.
Unable to resume pre-accident managerial employment and suffered reduced earning capacity.
